component.name: Quire
component.summary: A Soulver-style notepad calculator for Linux

description.p: Quire is a notepad calculator for the Wayland desktop: prose, markdown structure, and math share one plain-text sheet, and every expression answers on its own line in a results column at the right edge, live as you type.

Write sums the way you would say them: 200 + 15%, 15% of 200, milk = 3.50, total. Variables carry down the sheet, bare references answer with their value, a heading sections the math as well as the page, and lists continue themselves as you write. An error belongs to its line and never breaks the others.

Local-first and plain files: no accounts, no sync, no telemetry, and no live prices, ever. Sheets are plain UTF-8 that any editor can open. Kanagawa Dragon and Lotus themes ship built in, along with the bundled JetBrains Mono face.

screenshot.caption: A sheet with variables, percentages, and the live answers column

description.p: The &N renumber cascade fix: references renumber in place without viewport jumps or ref corruption.
Mixed-line evaluation, recursive multi-clause functions, and the &N renumbering wiring.
The &N renumbering wiring lands: references follow their targets as lines shift.
Stable line references, mixed-line evaluation, and token-level error highlighting.
Functions reach the unit engine: unit lines call user functions, dimension-checked by numbat.
The productivity wave: units, currency, dates, tags, functions, dated price snapshots, shipped portfolio and budget templates, the answer-decimals setting, and result format cycling.

First tagged release: the quire-eval engine (arithmetic, the four percent forms, variables, answer, heading-or-total bounded totals, span-carrying errors), the GTK4 sheet editor with the live answers column, Kanagawa Dragon and Lotus themes, the document backbone (open, save, recents, dirty guard, file monitoring), and the editing UX (outline, Tab completion, copy-answer, definition jump, drag-and-drop open, line numbers, list continuation).
